LESSON: TALK ABOUT

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: Effective By the end of the sub-strand, the  Learners listen to stories and ide
Topic 1.4: Talk about

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Talk about. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify messages conveyed in a thematic story and engage in oral discussions
2. use appropriate expressions to describe people, situations, and events
3. build on one’s ideas in a conversation by linking them to those given by others
4. develop an interest to read stories and texts.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify messages conveyed in a thematic story and engage in oral discussions
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to identify messages conveyed in a thematic story and engage in oral discussions. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. use appropriate expressions to describe people, situations, and events
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to use appropriate expressions to describe people, situations, and events. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. build on one’s ideas in a conversation by linking them to those given by others
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to build on one’s ideas in a conversation by linking them to those given by others. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

4. develop an interest to read stories and texts.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to develop an interest to read stories and texts. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Talk about using something you see at school.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Talk about.
2. Explain Talk about to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Talk about.
4. Show that you can: identify messages conveyed in a thematic story and engage in oral discussions
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Talk about. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Talk about important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. identify messages conveyed in a thematic story and engage in oral discussions
2. use appropriate expressions to describe people, situations, and events
3. build on one’s ideas in a conversation by linking them to those given by others
4. develop an interest to read stories and texts.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
